claims.claim: Eustathius of Antioch was Patriarch of Antioch from 324 to 330.
Eustathius of Antioch was born at Side in Pamphylia.
Eustathius of Antioch died c. 337 at Traianopolis in Thrace.
Eustathius of Antioch was bishop of Beroea before becoming patriarch of Antioch.
The Commentary on the Hexameron attributed to Eustathius is actually an anonymous work written between 375 and 500 AD.
The work could not have been written by Eustathius of Antioch because it draws from Basil the Great's Homilies on the Hexameron delivered around 370, after Eustathius's death.
More than 26 medieval manuscripts of the work exist, all of which give Eustathius of Antioch as the author.
The work contains historical material down to the time of Alexander the Great and has been given the Latin title Liber chronicorum ('book of chronicles').
The work includes extracts from the lost writings of Alexander Polyhistor, and the author appears to have had direct access to copies of Polyhistor.
The work is a useful early witness to the Physiologus.
Eusebius of Caesarea is labelled 'holy' in the work, despite being an enemy of Eustathius of Antioch.
The text was composed in the late 4th-early 5th century and makes use of Basil the Great's work on the same subject, as well as Josephus and Achilles Tatius.
